newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rockwell expands its business in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Rockwell expands its business in Russia.

text.p: U.S. Rockwell International announced on Friday its first joint production contracts with two Russian firms which develop and manufacture avionics.

Clayton Jones, vice president of Collins Commercial Avionics, a unit of Rockwell, told a news conference his company had signed contracts with the Elara avionics firm from Central Russia and the Moscow-based Gosnias research institute.
"Under these contracts Collins will provide basic components to Elara and then purchase completed aircraft systems control system (ASCS) units from Elara," Jones said.
Gosnias will develop the software and sell it to Collins.

Jones said that Rockwell's total investments in Russian projects were about $100 million. This included $50 million invested by Collins Commercial Avionics in a project to develop a new Russian-made Ilyushin-96M airliner powered by U.S.-made engines.
Earlier this year, Russian carrier Aeroflot ordered 15 collision-avoidance systems from Collins after the airline had already bought 30 units at a cost of about $15 million.
Aeroflot plans to equip a total of 50 planes with the system.
